title: The librarian who measured the Earth with a stick
hook: A librarian measured the whole Earth using only a stick.
summary: Around 240 BC, Eratosthenes compared shadows in two Egyptian cities and calculated the Earth's size, possibly within a few percent, without leaving Egypt.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Wikipedia 'Eratosthenes': head of the Library of Alexandria, measured Earth's circumference using shadow angles at Syene and Alexandria, about one fiftieth of a circle.

Cleomedes, 'On the Circular Motions of the Celestial Bodies' (preserves the method); modern scholars say the accuracy depends on the length of the stadion, so estimates of error range from about 1 to 16 percent.

lines.text: A librarian measured the whole Earth using only a stick.
Around two hundred forty BC, Eratosthenes ran the Library of Alexandria.
He heard that in Syene, the noon sun shone straight down a well.
lines.caps: In *Syene, | the noon *sun | shone down a *well

lines.text: But in Alexandria, the same day, a stick still cast a shadow.
lines.caps: But in *Alexandria, | a *stick | still cast a *shadow

lines.text: So the Earth had to curve, by about one fiftieth of a circle.
lines.caps: So the Earth *curves, | one *fiftieth | of a *circle

lines.text: He multiplied the distance between the cities by fifty.

image.search: Eratosthenes measurement of Earth circumference diagram

lines.text: Some estimates say he was off by only a few percent.
He never left Egypt to do it.

post.caption:
Two thousand years before satellites, a shadow weighed the world.
Could you have worked it out with just a stick?
Follow @unt.oldfiles for a new untold story every day.
